question: What will be the maximum intraday value of the VIX over these biweekly periods in Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Spot VIX 17.20 (Sep 15, FRED) after a week of rising rates/oil and an AI-capex repricing; the window (Sep 21-Oct 2, 10 trading days) opens after today's FOMC, where a 25bp hike is ~94% priced, so the dominant path is a post-event vol crush toward 15-16 with the max intraday print set by a single risk-off day. Reference-class median ratio ~1.16x on 17.20 gives ~20.0; I shade the median slightly below that to 19.6 for mean reversion off an elevated spot, then keep a fat right tail because the setup carries genuine regime-break candidates in both directions: 10y through 5%, Brent >$105, a Fed starting a hiking cycle into rich equity valuations, quarter-end on Sep 30, and the September jobs report on Oct 2 at 8:30 ET inside the window. Downside case is bounded: for the max to sit below ~17 VIX must fall and stay sub-16 for two straight weeks, which August showed is possible (max-high/start ratios of 1.04-1.07). No human market prices this contract (Polymarket/Manifold: none found by harness title search; Kalshi KXVIX series: no open markets; no bookmaker), so there is no crowd anchor and nothing to blend. Thin-evidence caveat: I could not retrieve a reliable recent VIX intraday-high series (Cboe CSV truncated, stooq empty, a Yahoo extraction returned values inconsistent with FRED closes and was discarded), so the high-vs-close gap is estimated (~4-7% on the max day) rather than measured.

calls.reconciliation: No web access on this run, so factual disputes were settled from the dossiers. (1) Anchor level: Runs 2 and 3 independently carry Sep 16 Investing.com OHLC (16.83/17.15/16.55) that Run 1 lacked; anchored at ~16.85 rather than Run 1's 17.20. (2) Close-to-high gap: Run 1 estimated +4-7% and applied it to close-derived base rates; Run 2 measured the relevant statistic (max-high vs max-close WITHIN a window) at 1.018, with per-day gaps averaging ~1.05. The measurement governs, so close-based ratios need only ~2% uplift, which lowers Run 1's implied median. (3) 2026 peak: Run 2's 'April spike to 52.33' conflicts with Runs 1/3 (~31-35 in March/April) and Run 3 separately dates a ~52 print to April 2025 - Run 2 most likely mis-assigned the year, so I hold 2026's high at ~31-35 and keep p_above_upper at 1% rather than inflating it. (4) Contango streak length (109 days as of Sep 11 vs 70 days as of Sep 1) is arithmetically inconsistent and could NOT be settled here; both runs agree the curve is in contango, which is the fact the forecast rests on, so the discrepancy carries no weight. (5) All three independently found no Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi/bookmaker contract - settled, no anchor. (6) The reference-class median ratio (1.16/1.22/1.17) is unverifiable model recall, a JUDGMENT dispute with no tie-breaker; I took ~1.18, near the cluster, and adopted Run 3's reference class and Run 1/3-style dispersion because I agree with them. The net of the settled facts (later, lower spot; smaller high-vs-close correction; 2026 not a 50-print year) puts me at or just below the lowest run median rather than between them - that is where the reconciled evidence lands, not a compromise. Unresolved and priced as uncertainty: the Sep 16 FOMC outcome and Warsh's press-conference tone, unknown to every run and to me, which sets the level the window opens from.
